PTP virtual clock topology and timestamp conversion rules beyond disabled fallback.
Random generator seeding, blocking behavior and architecture entropy sources.
Kernel stack randomization key lifecycle and boot configuration handling.
RAID parity algorithm selection and recovery behavior.
RAS daemon protocol, error decoding and DRAM retirement policy.
Core rate limit decision and window replenishment logic outside init and reset helpers.

findings.text: PTP driver descriptor holds ownership, printable name with fixed length limit, maximum frequency adjustment, counts for alarms external timestamps periodic outputs pins and loopback outputs, pulse per second presence, supported flag masks for periodic output and external timestamp, optional pin table pointer, plus driver callbacks for frequency and phase tuning, time and cycle reading in plain extended and cross forms, time setting, request enablement, pin validation, auxiliary work and loopback control.
Clock notification categories distinguish alarm expiry, external timestamp arrival, external offset report, kernel pulse per second event and user visible pulse per second event.
Event report carries numeric category and channel index plus a payload interpreted by category as either large unsigned timestamp, signed offset, or pulse timing structure.
Scaled parts per million conversion offsets input by one then scales by about one hundred twenty five over eight thousand using sixty four bit intermediate and shift, returning signed long result.

Scaled adjustment magnitude is proportional to base times absolute scaled rate divided by one million shifted by sixteen; helper reports whether original rate was negative, and caller subtracts magnitude for negative rates otherwise adds it.

When PTP support is configured out, registration yields null handle, unregistration reports success, event delivery and worker cancellation do nothing, index and pin lookup helpers report absence, and worker scheduling reports operation not supported.
Virtual clock index lookup and hardware to virtual timestamp translation in disabled configuration return zero.
System timestamp capture helpers are null tolerant and only sample snapshot for identifier stored in supplied structure.
Purgatory hash region descriptor is an address plus length pair using unsigned machine word fields.
Minimum disk count required for RAID6 operation is four.

Word sized random accessor follows machine word width, bounded unsigned helpers return zero for trivial ceilings and otherwise use width appropriate multiplication with rejection to avoid modulo bias with power of two fast path, above helper shifts range upward by floor plus one, inclusive helper shifts by floor, constant inputs are checked at build time.

Blocking byte helper waits for seeding then fills buffer and propagates wait status, virtual machine fork notifier registration helpers are inert success stubs in this configuration, latent entropy helper contributes CPU latent value when plugin present otherwise contributes empty input.

Stack offset randomization derives thirty two bit value from per CPU generator with proper CPU pairing, masks it to small aligned range with two build dependent widths, allocates that many bytes from stack area and pins allocation against optimization, interrupt disabled variant asserts disabled state and reads raw CPU pointer, disabled configuration expands to empty statements.

Address interval holds inclusive sixty four bit start and end, length adds unity to span between bounds, containment requires outer bounds to enclose inner bounds, overlap requires each start not beyond opposite end, construction macro builds value from two endpoints.
Translation error record bundles faulting address, identifier for reporting hardware block, and affected CPU number.

In this configuration reliability helpers are inert: user consumer count zero, debug and daemon trace setup do nothing, nonstandard and ARM error loggers return without action, DRAM row retirement does nothing, address conversion reports invalid argument, logical index mapping either masks hardware identifier before lookup or reports invalid argument depending on build.
Rate limit control block contains raw spin lock guarding mutable state, interval and burst limits, atomic counters for remaining budget and suppressed messages, flag word, and window start time.

Initialization clears object then sets lock interval and burst, default form uses compile time interval and burst, missed counter uses atomic increment read and exchange, interval reset takes interrupt saving lock updates interval clears initialized marker restores budget and clears missed count, release helper warns about suppressed lines only when release reporting flag is set.

Default rate limit window equals five timer units with burst of ten messages, release reporting uses lowest flag bit and initialized marker uses next bit, disabled initializer uses zero interval with default burst.

Rate limited warning helpers evaluate condition once and only emit when gate allows, using per call site persistent state in one spelling; alternate build removes gating and warns directly on condition.

Reciprocal divisor stores multiplier plus two small shift counts, extended form stores multiplier single shift exponent and wide flag, division helper combines scaled multiply with correction based on first shift then final shift.

Reference tracking directory when enabled holds spin lock, quarantine budget, two reference counts for untracked and missing tracker cases, liveness flag, active and quarantine lists, plus class name pointer; disabled build leaves structure empty.

Enabled initialization prepares both lists and lock, records quarantine budget and class, marks live, initializes reference counts to one and hooks debugging plus depot support; disabled initialization and exit print symlink helpers are empty with query returning zero.

Memory buffer cursor pairs current pointer with remaining length, zero and write helpers clamp request to remainder advance cursor and report leftover, offset helper returns clamped advanced view, store helper writes whole value or truncated prefix when space short and advances accordingly.

Register set descriptor provides callbacks for reading writing activity testing and writeback together with element count size alignment bias and core dump note identity derived from token, view aggregates name table pointer count and ELF machine flags ABI and operating system fields.

Register copy helper validates position against start, limits transfer to requested range, advances kernel or user source pointers plus destination position and remaining count and signals fault on bad user address; user copy helper checks fault context instruments operation injects configured failures validates destination size then delegates to raw copy and instruments result.

Rate limiter moves from uninitialized to armed window with full burst budget, consumes budget per emission while counting suppressed attempts as missed, starts new window after interval expiry, and optionally reports total suppressed count on teardown.

Several helpers silently truncate or assume valid inputs: bounded random requires non zero ceiling and narrower than full range for inclusive form, range length underflows if end precedes start, memory buffer helpers discard excess bytes without error, user register copy assumes caller maintains start invariant, PTP disabled stubs hide absence behind null or negative returns that callers must check.
